title: Gordie Howe bridge surpasses 1M vehicle crossings while other bridges, tunnel lose traffic
summary: The Gordie Howe International Bridge has seen more than a million crossings since it officially opened to vehicle traffic on July 27, according to new numbers from the Bridge and Tunnel Operators…

image.caption: The Gordie Howe International Bridge had seen 1,051,470 crossings as of Oct. 31. (Patrick Morrell/CBC)

blocks.text: Windsor

The Gordie Howe International Bridge has seen more than a million crossings since it officially opened to vehicle traffic on July 27, according to new numbers from the Bridge and Tunnel Operators Association.
Windsor-Detroit tunnel remains the most popular passenger vehicle crossing, CEO says
Meanwhile, vehicle traffic over the Ambassador and Blue Water bridges and through the Windsor-Detroit Tunnel has declined.
The numbers cover the first three full months since the Gordie Howe opened.
They show the bridge averaging around 248,000 passenger vehicle crossings per month and slightly fewer than 85,000 truck crossings.
In a statement, the Windsor-Detroit Bridge Authority said, too, that more than 48,000 pedestrians and cyclists had used the bridge's multi-use path.

"The Gordie Howe International Bridge supports the efficient and effective movement of traffic in the Windsor-Detroit gateway by providing additional capacity, crossing choice and highway-to-highway connectivity for travellers and commercial operators crossing the border," the statement read.
"We are encouraged by the continued interest in the bridge and the growth in traffic volumes as more users become familiar with the crossing."
Windsor-Detroit Tunnel crossings were down just shy of 19 per cent between Aug. 1 and Oct. 31, while crossings at the Blue Water Bridge in Sarnia were down approximately 12.5 per cent.
The Ambassador Bridge saw the biggest decline in total crossings — down nearly 32 per cent compared with the same period last year.
Tunnel CEO not surprised by numbers
Most of that decline was in passenger vehicle traffic, not truck traffic.

Truck crossings were off just 8.75 per cent since the same August-through-October period last year, despite hopes among some residents of Sandwich Town that the new bridge would ease traffic congestion on Huron Church Road.
Truck crossings at the Blue Water Bridge were down just over 30 per cent.
Windsor-Detroit Tunnel CEO Tal Czudner said he’s not surprised by the numbers.
Tunnel CEO Tal Czudner said he is happy to see the tunnel, which is jointly owned by the cities of Windsor and Detroit, remain the most popular passenger vehicle crossing. (CBC)

“[The Ambassador Bridge] had a very long runway to negotiate some very favorable deals with different … trucking companies. And obviously they own a decent amount of trucking infrastructure themselves.”

Truck crossings at the Ambassador Bridge remain up 3.85 per cent for the period running from Jan. 1 to the end of October, compared with the same period last year, while overall bridge traffic is down 6.82 per cent over the same time period.
Czudner said he is happy to see the tunnel, which is jointly owned by the cities of Windsor and Detroit, remain the most popular passenger vehicle crossing.
He also said the Windsor side of the operation has lost less traffic than the Detroit side.

“I think what you're finding is there's a lot of the people who work in automotive, manufacturing, healthcare, live in Windsor-Essex, take the tunnel to work, and then they take the Gordie Howe home,” he said.

“From a pricing perspective, that's actually the cheapest way to go. If you sign up for a [tunnel] Nexpress account, it’s the cheapest way to get from Windsor to Detroit. And if you sign up for a Breakaway account with Gordie Howe, that's the cheapest way to get from Detroit back to Windsor.”
